We are Playdead, an independent game company based in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. We have made two critically acclaimed titles, LIMBO and INSIDE. Our current project is a 3rd-person science fiction adventure set in a remote corner of the universe.

We are seeking an experienced Level Architect with strong artistic skills to join our team in Copenhagen. As our process is very visually driven, we expect layout artists to have a strong eye for visual composition and broad experience in the creation of 3D environments.

Your responsibility as our new colleague will be in designing, blocking out, and in some cases modeling locations for a third-person, open-world game. At Playdead, locations are often designed with a combination of grey-boxing and more detailed, modeled elements. You will work in coordination with the other designers and artists on the team with a focus on how the player will flow within the level and betweens spaces.

We are a close-knit group of developers, and working within that group requires an ability to adapt to the existing visual style and methods while contributing your own ideas to the whole. We are particularly looking for a candidate who enjoys setting their own goals and taking responsibility for their own schedule. More than anything, we are looking for someone who is excited about all facets of game development, as well as being passionate about gaming overall.

You should be willing to work at the Playdead office in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Keywords for position

layout - level design - composition -3D - modelling - iteration

What will you be doing?

• Level layout, spatial design and composition using primitive blockouts and 3D assets to produce believable locations within a large, open world.

• Taking a basic brief and mocking up a grey box design to set the foundation for further development and visual storytelling.

• Detailed, untextured 3D modeling

• Iterating on existing location designs based on feedback and testing.

• Collaborating with other artists and designers to support level design and construction.

If you wish to apply, please consider the following general requirements

• You have worked on the development of at least one released 3D game.

• A link to an online portfolio of previous work showcasing a knowledge of composition, layout, lighting, colour and visual storytelling.

• Experience with a game engine such as Unity, Unreal etc. or an internal engine is a must.

• Experience with 3D packages such as Blender, Maya, 3dsMax, etc. is a strong advantage.

Desired skills

• Experience with world creation tools such as World Machine, Quadspinner Gaea, or similar is a plus.

Who We Are

We are a team of more than 100 creative professionals. We experiment and collaborate with a focus on creating new experiences, and as such we are looking for people who can help us achieve them.

Our approach to development does not include crunching towards arbitrary deadlines - instead, we particularly look for talented people who enjoy managing their own schedule and thrive on working within a friendly, collaborative environment.

We love to make carefully crafted games with obsessive attention to detail and are always on the lookout for others who share that passion.

As an apprentice, you will also become part of a workplace where you learn by doing. You will work alongside experienced colleagues and gradually take on more responsibility as your skills develop.

What will you learn?

As a Crane Mechanic Apprentice, you will work with the construction, installation, troubleshooting and repair of truck-mounted cranes and truck chassis.

Modern cranes combine mechanics with advanced electrical, hydraulic and electronic systems, so two days are not quite the same.

During your apprenticeship, you will gain practical experience with:

• Chassis Construction and modification

• Truck-mounted cranes

• Hydraulic systems

• Electrical and electronic systems

• Diagnostics and fault finding

• Welding and metalworking

• CAD and technical drawings

• Control and monitoring systems

• Commissioning and calibration

• Safety inspections

You will also learn to use computers and specialist software for diagnostics, commissioning and calibration.

About the programme

The Crane Mechanic programme takes 4 years and combines school-based training with practical apprenticeship training in a company.

The programme starts with Basic Course 2, lasting 20 weeks. You then continue to the main course, where school periods at HEG alternate with practical training in your apprenticeship company.

At the end of the programme, you complete your final trade examination and become a qualified Crane Mechanic.

Who are we looking for?

You do not need to know everything from day one – that is what the apprenticeship is for.

• Has completed compulsory schooling (lower secondary education)

• Has a legal right to work on Denmark at the start of employment without the need for a work permit

jobs.occupation: Backend Developer, Data Collection and Infrastructure
jobs.description:
What we are building

Someone researching a purchase might start in ChatGPT, compare options in Perplexity, run a Google search, then go back to an AI assistant to decide. The companies being compared have little idea where they show up in that chain or what gets said about them, and very few can measure it today.

We build the infrastructure that measures it. Every platform we track changes under us, and none of them offers a feed, so we collect the data ourselves. The collection is the hard part, and it is most of this job. Three products run on it:

• AccuRanker is the rank tracking and SEO analytics platform. Rankings, competitor movement, keyword research, dashboards, forecasting.

• AccuLLM tracks brand visibility inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overview, and AI Mode.

• AccuSERP is a search data API we sell to other companies in the industry.

On a normal day that means 27 billion rows inserted, 85 million web requests collected, 80 million background jobs run, and 64 million analytical queries served. Eight people build and run all of it.

What you will work on

• The collection and ingestion pipeline behind those numbers, together with the engineers who run it today.

• Add coverage for new search surfaces as they appear, and fix the ones we already cover when they change shape.

• Write and tune queries against very large time series data, across columnar and relational stores.

• Start with scoped changes to existing services, and grow into owning services yourself, from design through deployment to how they behave in production.

What you bring

Must have:

• Solid programming fundamentals. You write clear code and can reason about what it costs at runtime.

• Code of yours running somewhere real. A production system at work, a service you host yourself, or a side project with actual users.

• Comfort in Linux. You can read logs, follow a request through a system, and find out why something is slow.

• Ownership. You take a problem, decide how to attack it, ask when you are stuck, and follow through.

Good to have:

• Distributed systems fundamentals. Queues, workers, backpressure, etc.

• Python and its common frameworks (Django, Celery, pandas/polars). Our stack runs mostly on Python, but it is not a must if the fundamentals are strong.

• ClickHouse or another columnar store.

• The network layer. Connection lifecycle, timeouts and retries, TLS, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

• Web scraping or browser automation.

• AI agents. Tool and context design, structured output and evals.

• Kafka.

All of it can be learned here.

Who does well here

People who set a high standard for their own work, and who care about performance, reliability, cost, and operational simplicity.

You want to own a feature end to end, from idea to production. The problems we hand you will be scoped at first, and less so over time, and a month after something ships, you are still the one who cares about it.

You move fast when speed is what the problem needs, and you know when stability, safety and maintainability matter more.

This field moves fast right now. We expect you to read, try things, and form your own view of what is worth using, without waiting to be told what is new.

The job is wide. In one week you might tune a database, debug a proxy network, and design an agent.

This role is not for you if you want a narrow technical scope or a large team around you. We are small, the problems change, and you will get real responsibility earlier than most places give it. The senior engineers sit next to you, and asking them is part of the job.

AI at AccuRanker

AI is a big part of the product and of how we build it. AccuLLM sends queries to LLMs all day, customers use our MCP server, and agents and tool design are real engineering problems here.

Being effective with coding agents is becoming a core engineering skill, and it is part of this job. You should be good at giving agents the right context, breaking work into pieces they can execute well, reviewing what they produce, and knowing when to take over yourself. The bar is more high-quality engineering done without outsourcing your understanding and judgment, which is a different thing from using AI a lot.

How we work

• You own services, not tickets. You decide how to solve the problem, make the tradeoffs, and deploy it yourself.

• We ship many times a day. A change can go from idea to production the same day.

• We argue about designs, in writing and in the room. Correctness, cost, and latency are worth arguing about out loud.

• We share what we know and help each other own unfamiliar parts of the system.

What we offer

• Salary set individually on skills and experience.

• Pension, health insurance, flexible working hours, and paid parental leave.

• Hardware of your choosing.

• Office in central Aarhus on Åboulevarden, top floors, panoramic views over the city. The role is on-site, with hybrid options planned for later this year.

• Great lunch.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note to pet@accuranker.com, in Danish or English. A link to something you have built counts for a lot.

We review applications as they come in and hire as soon as we find the right person, so send yours when it is ready.

Questions about the role are welcome. Call our CTO, Peter Emil Tybirk, on +45 61 41 77 41.

We are moving our entire network and firewall estate to an automated, code-driven operating model, and we need someone who can help lead that shift. If Ansible, Terraform and Git workflows excite you more than console access, this role is built for you.

**The job

**

You will help design, build and operate the automation platform behind our entire network and firewall estate, moving us from manual, device-by-device changes to a version-controlled, peer-reviewed, GitOps-style way of working. As a technical anchor in Core Infrastructure Platforms, you will shape how the whole Infrastructure department approaches network automation.

In short, you can look forward to:

•    Driving network automation – help architecting, building and maintaining network automation for our Cisco and Palo Alto estate, replacing manual configuration with automated deployments.

•    Owning our network Source of Truth – building and operating the authoritative, version-controlled model of our intended network state (think Nautobot or Infrahub).

•    Designing CI/CD and Git – setting up pull requests, automated checks and review-gated deployments, and running the platforms

•    Running core network and SDN infrastructure – owning and optimising our datacenter and enterprise network, including Software-Defined Networking

**Joining the team

**

You will join our Infrastructure department, a small team coving everything infrastructure related.  We are in the beginning   of an ambitious shift from manual device configuration to a Source of Truth-driven, GitOps-style operating model, and you will have real influence over the architecture, tooling and practices we adopt next.

You will also act as a sparring partner and mentor to colleagues across Infrastructure, sharing what you build through documentation and peer review so good ideas do not stay with just one person.

**Your qualifications

**

You have a solid networking foundation combined with hands-on experience in modern network automation. You are comfortable working across Cisco and Palo Alto platforms, treating infrastructure as code with tools such as Ansible or Terraform, building CI/CD pipelines and using Git. •    Solid networking fundamentals (L2/L3, BGP, OSPF, EVPN, VXLAN) with hands-on experience in Cisco (IOS/NX-OS) and Palo Alto/Panorama, plus exposure to SDN paradigms such as Cisco ACI.

•    Hands-on experience with Ansible or Terraform applied to network infrastructure.

•    Experience designing or operating CI/CD pipelines and using Git

Are you passionate about data and driven by the opportunity to make a real impact by helping companies turn facts into actionable insights? Do you thrive in dynamic environments where you work with some of the most complex and modern data solutions? If so, you might be our next colleague.

Responsibilities & technologies

In Data Management, you will become part of a team that contributes to enabling our customers to develop and manage their business based on data and knowledge.

You will work in the intersection of technology and business. Information and data are at the core of our work, and we can see that our analyses, advice, and final solutions create value for our customers. The work involves developing technical solutions to collect, process, model, analyze, and visualize data.

To provide the best possible advice and support to our customers, we place great importance on staying up to date with the latest trends and technologies in data management. You will work with a broad range of market-leading technologies, including: Azure SQL Server, Snowflake, dbt, Microsoft SQL Server, and others.

Your tasks are highly varied and depend on your skills and the direction you wish to develop.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Design, modeling, and building of data structures such as databases.

• Structuring and collection of data from various sources.

• Implementation of business logic on data for use in reporting.

• Customer advisory, strategy work, and business analysis in collaboration with our customers.

• Development of reports for business users with a focus on front-end.

About you

You are newly graduated or have up to a couple of years of relevant professional experience within data management. Through your education, you have gained a solid professional foundation and a logical approach to handling complex data and challenges. You thrive in a development-oriented environment with a focus on collaboration and continuous personal and professional development.

To succeed in this role, you have experience with or the interest to learn:

• ETL and Database technologies.

• Languages such as various versions of SQL, Python, and R.

• Business Intelligence tools: Power BI, Tableau, and others.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must.
